(Mohamad & Dr. Yusra, 2023) conducted a study to investigating the impact of 
mobile applications on academic performance; their finding mostly aligns with 
the aforementioned effects of MOOCs. By improving student engagement, 
academic performance, and enablement of self-directed learning. The paper did 
report that students’ perception of the app’s effectiveness varied.  
2.4.5 Collaborative and Social Learning Tools 
In 2.3.6 the effect of collaborative group work is discussed and showed promise 
in providing students with an effective learning strategy. 
A paper by (Kyparisia & Maria, 2011) looks into the effects of collaborative 
learning on eLearning platforms. Students were grouped and were asked to 
create a product within an eLearning environment, this involved the students 
creating ideas, researching, discussing and developing the project. The study 
found, asynchronous forums for communication, and shared databases, key 
factors towards the project’s success. These technologies were found to increase 
the frequency of peer learning opportunities, provide an environment for 
negotiation and debate; which improved overall student performance. The paper 
did highlight that this is not a one-size-fits-all, with students from different 
backgrounds exhibiting varied responses.
